items.item_text: 01. Which option below best describes your highest level of education? (NOTE: For positions requiring college units/degree, a copy of the transcript must be included as an attachment. The transcript must be legible from an accredited institution and include your name, the institution name and confer date). Options: Some High School | High School or G.E.D. | Some College | Associates Degree | Bachelors Degree | Masters Degree | Doctorate Degree | None
02. Did you attach the required certifications? Options: Yes | No
03. Select the career website you used to find this employment opportunity: Options: Sbccd.edu | Indeed.com | HigherEdJobs.com | EdJoin.org | CCCregistry.org | Other

04. Describe your experience supporting NCAA, 3C2A/CCCAA, and/or high school athletic programs. Include the institution(s), level of competition, dates of experience, and your primary responsibilities.

05. Describe your experience using electronic medical record (EMR) and/or athletic injury tracking systems. Include the names of the systems used, the length of time you used them, and the functions you performed.

06. Describe your experience coordinating care with physicians and other healthcare providers. Include the types of cases handled, your role in communication, referrals, treatment coordination, and return-to-play decisions

07. Describe your experience providing athletic training coverage for multiple sports, traveling with teams, and transporting athletic training equipment to practices, competitions, and other athletic events. Include the types of sports supported, the type of equipment transported, frequency of travel and transportation responsibilities, and the types of vehicles operated.

08. I hereby understand and declare that the statements on this supplemental questionnaire are true and complete to the best of my knowledge. As applicable, I hereby authorize the District and/or designees to contact the references listed to verify the information I have supplied. I hereby release from liability all persons and organizations furnishing such information. I understand that the District reserves the right to validate information received on the supplemental questionnaire and that I will be subject to disqualification and/or termination if any statement in this supplemental questionnaire is found to be untrue or determined to be misleading. Options: Yes | No
Possession of and ability to maintain a current Board of Certification for Athletic Training Certificate (BOC ATC).
Possession of current CPR Certificate and First Aid certifications.
Possession of a valid driver’s license.
Two (2) years of experience working as a certified athletic trainer at the secondary level or higher.
1 year Experience supporting NCAA/3C2A athletic programs, or 3 years' experience supporting High School level athletic programs.
Experience with electronic medical record and injury tracking system.
Evaluates athletic injuries, performs appropriate first aid, provides and coordinates referrals to physicians, specialists, health services, hospitals, and other health professionals as necessary.
Administers follow-up treatment and rehabilitation based on the physician’s guidance and the trainer’s discretion.

Coordinates, develops, and administers post-surgical, preventative, and maintenance rehabilitation programs for student athletes utilizing various rehabilitative techniques, skills, and modalities prescribed by standing orders from the medical physician.

Develops, organizes, schedules, and implements preventative treatment methods, including but not limited to Physical Examinations, Emergency Action Plans (EAP’s), and concussion management protocols in accordance with CCCAA requirements and guidelines.
Applies taping and wrapping of injured areas and for injury surveillance.
Assists in the coordination of travel arrangements for the athletic trainers, medical equipment, and potential medical care for out-of-town athletic events.
Inspects practice and competition areas to ensure safety and injury prevention.
Attends games and renders first aid and immediate evaluation of injuries as necessary.
Ensures Athletic Training Room is open and training services are available whenever intercollegiate teams are practicing or competing on campus.

Maintains confidential records, including injury report forms, diagnoses, treatment, prescriptions, physical examination reports, accident reports, and insurance forms as related to the athletics program.
Operates whirlpool, ultrasound, hydrocollator, muscle stimulator, and other exercise and therapeutic machines.
Communicates with coaches, athletes, team physicians, and others regarding injuries, treatments, and rehabilitation programs.
Coordinates and consults with coaches to design off-season physical conditioning programs for athletes requiring physical rehabilitation.
Orders, receives, and stocks training supplies, equipment, and materials as needed.
Maintains current knowledge of athletic training trends and practices; incorporates new developments as appropriate into program.
